text.p: -- Salomon Bros said analyst John Jones raised his recommendation on Stratus Computer Inc to strong buy from buy.
-- Shares were up 1-1/2 to 21-1/4 on the New York Stock Exchange.
-- Jones also put the stock's 12-month price target at $30 per share.

-- In his research note, Jones said Stratus' current share price is "very compelling" since the stock has fallen recently because of "disappointing June-quarter results and a lack of company guidance to the street."

-- They expect Stratus to exceed the $0.42 per share consensus estimate for the September quarter. "The company should meet or exceed our estimate of $0.48 per share (for the September quarter) and our 1996 and 1997 earnings per share of $2.05 and $2.75, respectively," Jones said.

-- "We have a high degree of confidence in the company's ability to sustain a healthy fault-tolerant computer business, return its software business to profitability, and reap the rewards from the substantial investments it made in creating a new growth business in the high-availability computer market -- an endeavor that has taken ten months longer to complete than originally planned," Jones said.

-- "If all else fails, at current valuations, Stratus becomes a take-out candidate for either Hewlett-Packard or Lucent Technologies, both companies are logically tied to Stratus' fault-tolerent platform."
